entries.title: Sky sign Kate Martin to development contract
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> signed Kate Martin to a development contract, the team announced Wednesday. Martin had a promising first two seasons in the WNBA but hasn't struck on a roster this season. She was cut by the Valkyries at the beginning of the year and then signed to a development contract by the Sparks, who later waived her. </p><p>In her rookie season with the Aces she shot 35.5% from three. She was then selected by the Valkyries in the 2025 expansion draft, where she became a key piece of their bench rotation. </p><p>The Sky have only four regular season games remaining, but the benefit of signing a development player now is they will retain her rights for next season.</p><p>They had one development spot open after forward Maddy Westebeld was poached by the Mercury.</p>
entries.author: Alissa Hirsh

entries.title: When Sides Collide matchups revealed
entries.summary: <p>Last season’s 27 wins were the most Lockport basketball has won in four decades and marked the first 20-win season since 2011. With the bulk of that team returning, there is plenty of hope — bordering hype — for this upcoming season.</p><p>An experienced group fresh off a strong summer and with high expectations this winter, coach Dave Wilson’s team will vault into the preseason Super 25 this November. The preseason expectations also open the door for another big opportunity.</p><p>While the Porters have been a regular at the prestigious Pontiac Holiday Tournament for many years, they’ve been absent from other high-profile events. But with the release of the matchups for the annual When Sides Collide event, Lockport gets a chance to play on a big stage.</p><p>“We are honored and grateful to compete in a great event and on the same stage with such notable programs,” Wilson said.</p><p>Wilson, who was hired in 2023 after nine years as head coach at Andrew, points out this is the first class he’s been with all the way through their four years at Lockport. They took on Wilson’s immediate program mindset, including the mantra, “How we do anything is how we do everything.”</p><p>“Be disciplined in the classroom and the weight room, be competitive and tenacious in practice, be diligent in film study and in being a good teammate," Wilson said. “They have done that. And to be included in this event is incredibly rewarding for this group that has given the school, coaching staff and community everything they have.”</p><p>Here are the matchups for this year’s When Sides Collide on January 23 at Benet.</p><h3>Mount Carmel vs. Oswego</h3><p>The opener brings several young, talented pieces together with Mount Carmel’s sophomore tandem of Ronald Johnson and DK Heard and Oswego juniors Ethan Vahl and 6-10 Cole Jansons.</p><h3>Bolingbrook vs. Neuqua Valley</h3><p>The state’s two best players — Bolingbrook’s Brady Pettigrew and Neuqua Valley’s Cole Kelly— meet again. Throw in Illinois recruit Mason Martin, arguably the state’s best shooter, and the fact both teams will be highly ranked again, and it’s possibly the marquee matchup of the season.</p><h3>Evanston vs. Lockport</h3><p>With four returning starters back from a 27-win team, including junior guard Ben Ojala, perennial power Evanston is loaded. Upstart Lockport, led by twins Nojus and Nedas Venckus, will have a lot of eyes on it as the Porters get a shot at a highly-ranked team in a premier event.</p><h3>Benet vs. East St. Louis</h3><p>A fresh face from the southern part of the state heads to the Chicago area as the defending Class 3A state champs look to repeat. The Flyers will have their hands full with Benet’s Ed Stasys and the always-raucous atmosphere.</p><h3>Team Rose Shootout matchups set</h3><p>An early-season event that will draw plenty of eyes is the annual Team Rose Chicagoland Shootout.</p><p>This massive 32-team event, which is spread out over three days, will bring several ranked teams and top prospects to Mount Carmel on Dec. 11-13.</p><p>Some of the highlight matchups include Marist vs. Kenwood, Romeoville vs. Evanston, St. Ignatius vs. Bolingbrook, St. Laurence vs. Neuqua Valley and Mount Carmel vs. Homewood-Flossmoor. </p>

entries.title: CPS students ordered to stay indoors during extreme heat warning
entries.summary: <p>All outdoor activities for Chicago Public Schools students have been canceled or will be held inside if possible due to the extreme and dangerous heat Wednesday, according to a letter addressed to families. </p><p>The order, put into effect due to the National Weather Service's heat advisory, includes outdoor recess, physical education, athletics and out-of-school time activities, <a class="Link" href="https://www.cps.edu/media/community-updates/2026/august/important-information-heat-advisory/" target="_blank" >according to the letter</a>. </p><p>The heat advisory remains in force until 9 p.m., according to the NWS. </p><p>The letter continued with information about air conditioning and warnings to stay hydrated. </p><p>"As a reminder, all CPS classrooms are equipped with air conditioning, and the CPS facilities team will be working with schools to fix any air conditioning systems that may encounter issues this week," the letter said. </p><p>CPS officials recommend students bring full water bottles to school. Students will be able to refill those bottles throughout the day, according to the letter. </p><p>A CPS "heat action plan" kicks in during extreme weather, according to the letter, which includes the following steps: <br></p><ul class="ul1" id="rte-11fe9c60-a6e0-11f1-9fce-1f79cb8bb21d"><li>Ensure that staff and students remain sufficiently hydrated</li><li>Ensure that all water fountains work.</li><li>Encourage and allow students to bring full water bottles to school and provide them with opportunities to refill them.</li><li>Monitor students taking particular medications to ensure proper hydration.</li><li>Keep rooms cool</li><li>Close shades in rooms to block sunlight.</li><li>Keep air circulating by opening windows and doors and using fans.</li><li>Turn off overhead lights, computers and appliances when not required for instruction.</li><li>Move classes from rooms exposed to sunlight and gather inauditoriums or rooms on the interior or in a lower level.</li></ul>

entries.title: Dolton woman accused in deadly DUI wreck in Avondale that killed passenger last year
entries.summary: <p>A Dolton woman was driving impaired and recklessly when she caused a deadly crash last year, police said. </p><p>Shana Weems, 32, has been charged with aggravated DUI and reckless homicide in the death of her passenger, 31-year-old Shanna Monique Quilter. The wreck occurred in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2025/12/08/passenger-dies-in-avondale-wreck-involving-semi" target="_blank" >3800 block of West Diversey Avenue on Dec. 8, 2025</a> in the city's Avondale neighborhood.</p><p>Quilter, of the Hermosa neighborhood, was ejected from the car and she died on the scene after the car Weems was driving smashed into two vehicles including a semi, police said at the time. </p><p>Weems is scheduled for a detention hearing Wednesday at the Leighton Criminal Courthouse. <br></p>

entries.title: Big Ten football preview: Ohio State, Oregon or Indiana at the top? Where do Illinois, Northwestern come in?
entries.summary: <p>I’m not about to remind you how badly I blew it with my <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/college-sports" target="_blank" >Big Ten</a> football preview last season.</p><p>If I did, I’d have to admit I not only <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/college-sports/2025/08/22/big-ten-preview-ohio-state-penn-state-oregon-michigan-illinois-college-football-playoff" target="_blank" >failed to see Indiana’s greatness coming</a> — Curt Cignetti’s destroyers set the new bar for all national title contenders, going 16-0 — but actually had the Hoosiers missing the College Football Playoff altogether.</p><p>Talk about an indefensible whiff. Luckily for me, I’ve already moved on to the present.</p><p>Opening games are here for every team in the Big Ten except for USC, which is 1-0 after an extra-early creampuff win. The Trojans have eyes on a playoff breakthrough, but who doesn’t?</p><p>I’ve gone game-by-game through the schedule to predict this order of finish, which factors in the 18-team conference’s absurdly complicated tiebreaker rules insofar as a person of moderate intelligence and a growing desire to think about lunch can understand them.</p><p>Here’s how it’s all going to play out:</p><h3><b>1. Ohio State</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>12-2 overall, 9-0 Big Ten.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>11-1, 9-0.</p><p><b>THE BUCKEYES</b> have veteran quarterback Julian Sayin, all-world receiver Jeremiah Smith, stud running back Bo Jackson, four-fifths of last year’s starting offensive line, NFL players at every level on defense and the nation’s No. 1 ranking going in. The schedule is an absolute monster, though, with all the heaviest hitters on it. A Week 2 mega-test at Texas will help, win or lose, down the line.</p><h3><b>2. Oregon</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>13-2, 8-1.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>11-1, 8-1.</p><p><b>THE DUCKS </b>are the only conference foe that goes toe-to-toe with Ohio State at spending on talent. That and having a QB, Dante Moore, who can carry the team on his back in a tough environment (see: at Penn State last season) are two of the reasons the Ducks have as good a shot at getting to the playoff as anybody. Can they win it, though? Finding the necessary level of brute physicality is the only step left.</p><h3><b>3. Michigan</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>9-4, 7-2.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>9-3, 7-2.</p><p><b>THE WOLVERINES </b>might need a minute to hit their stride under a new, Kyle Whittingham-led coaching staff, which is why I have them losing early to Oklahoma but beating Indiana at the Big House in late October. No such luck later on at Oregon or at Ohio State, though.</p><h3><b>4. Indiana</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>16-0, 9-0.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>10-2, 7-2.</p><p><b>THE HOOSIERS </b>can’t just plug-and-play like they’re peak Alabama, Georgia or Ohio State, can they? No, really, can they? There isn’t an abundance of skill production back from the Fernando Mendoza-led offense that cashed in seemingly every single time it needed a touchdown last season. Transfer QB Josh Hoover is the real deal, but Mendoza was a gem.</p><h3><b>5. USC</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>9-4, 7-2.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>9-3, 6-3.</p><p><b>THE TROJANS </b>took an important leap from Year 1 to Year 2 in the conference. The next move is to contend for the top spot in the conference. Oregon and Ohio State have to go to Los Angeles for what could be the biggest couple of games there since Lincoln Riley arrived. Alas, I have USC losing both those games as well as the one at Indiana.</p><h3><b>6. Washington</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>9-4, 5-4.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>8-4, 5-4.</p><p><b>THE HUSKIES </b>are going to be extremely tough to beat in Seattle, but are they ready to take their A-Game with them on the road more consistently? Last year’s total dud at Wisconsin — inexcusable — cost them a shot at 10 wins.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-af0000" name="image-af0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/431ecce/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3264x1832+0+0/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fd8%2F6c%2Fe0a77b3c451892cff786499af56a%2Fap25217778761525.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/0a22ba5/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3264x1832+0+0/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fd8%2F6c%2Fe0a77b3c451892cff786499af56a%2Fap25217778761525.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/9c46c75/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3264x1832+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fd8%2F6c%2Fe0a77b3c451892cff786499af56a%2Fap25217778761525.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Illinois football coach Bret Bielema talks with an official during the Citrus Bowl against South Carolina on Dec. 31, 2024, in Orlando, Florida. " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/9c46c75/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3264x1832+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fd8%2F6c%2Fe0a77b3c451892cff786499af56a%2Fap25217778761525.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/1e9b3b5/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3264x1832+0+0/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fd8%2F6c%2Fe0a77b3c451892cff786499af56a%2Fap25217778761525.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/9c46c75/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3264x1832+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fd8%2F6c%2Fe0a77b3c451892cff786499af56a%2Fap25217778761525.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Illinois football coach Bret Bielema talks with an official during the Citrus Bowl against South Carolina on Dec. 31, 2024, in Orlando, Florida. </p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Phelan M. Ebenhack/AP</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p></p><h3><b>7. Illinois</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>9-4, 5-4.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>8-4, 5-4.</p><p><b>THE ILLINI </b>are eighth on the “others receiving votes” list in the preseason AP poll, a far cry from how they were perceived heading in a year ago, but a 5-1 start — book it — will at least give this team a shot at accomplishing something big. Will Bret Bielema ever have the dominant line play he seeks?</p><h3><b>8. Penn State</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>7-6, 3-6.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>8-4, 5-4.</p><p><b>THE NITTANY LIONS’ </b>have a dream schedule, which has some getting cute and picking them to get back to the playoff in Matt Campbell’s first season as coach. Possible? Sure, but the transfers Campbell brought with him from Iowa State will have to deliver at the highest level.</p><h3><b>9. Iowa</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>9-4, 6-3.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>7-5, 4-5.</p><p><b>THE HAWKEYES </b>very rarely win fewer than eight games, but this team is a candidate for it. There is so little experience on offense, it’s scary.</p><h3><b>10. Minnesota</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>8-5, 5-4.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>7-5, 4-5.</p><p><b>THE GOPHERS </b>might have to win a few games in November just to pull themselves into the bowl picture. Better than the middle of the pack would be surprising and impressive.</p><h3><b>11. Maryland</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>4-8, 1-8.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>6-6, 4-5.</p><p><b>THE TERRAPINS </b>have losable non-conference games against UConn and Virginia Tech and trips to Nebraska and Ohio State early in league play. Coach Mike Locksley could be cooked.</p><h3><b>12. UCLA</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>3-9, 3-6.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>5-7, 4-5.</p><p><b>THE BRUINS’ </b>hopes in new coach Bob Chesney are riding on the Cignetti model: Win big at James Madison, bring a lot of transfers with you to a Power 4 school and shock the masses. We’ll see.</p><h3><b>13. Northwestern</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>7-6, 4-5.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>6-6, 3-6.</p><p><b>THE WILDCATS </b>need their new stadium to be a game changer. But having Indiana, Oregon and Ohio State all on the road? That’s criminal.</p><h3><b>14. Nebraska</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>7-6, 4-5.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>6-6, 3-6.</p><p><b>THE HUSKERS </b>have been under .500 in Big Ten play all three seasons under Matt Rhule and nine in a row overall. What else is new?</p><h3><b>15. Wisconsin</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>4-8, 2-7.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>5-7, 3-6.</p><p><b>THE BADGERS’ </b>Luke Fickell would love to have Locksley’s job security. Badgers fans won’t ever forget the “Air Raid” fiasco.</p><h3><b>16. Michigan State</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>4-8, 1-8.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>3-9, 2-7.</p><p><b>THE SPARTANS </b>are far behind in personnel in Year 1 of the Pat Fitzgerald era. Let the build begin. Northwestern at MSU in October will be intense.</p><h3><b>17. Rutgers</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>5-7, 2-7.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>4-8, 1-8.</p><p><b>THE SCARLET KNIGHTS </b>often are a little better than it seems they should be, and this might be one of those seasons. So they’ve got that going for them.</p><h3><b>18. Purdue</b></h3><p><b>2025: </b>2-10, 0-9.</p><p><b>2026 regular-season prediction: </b>2-10, 1-8.</p><p><b>THE BOILERMAKERS </b>have added a couple of 7-footers … wait, never mind, that’s basketball.</p>

entries.title: 'Broadview 6' scandal won't derail trial of CBP agent accused of 'gunpoint sexual assaults'
entries.summary: <p>A federal judge on Wednesday<b> </b>rejected<b> </b>the argument that the “Broadview Six” scandal involving alleged government misconduct should derail the prosecution of an immigration officer accused of sexual assault and facing trial<b> </b>next week.</p><p>U.S. Customs and Border Protection officer<b> </b>Luis<b> </b>Uribe<b> </b>pointed out<b> </b>last week<b> </b>that <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2025/12/09/ohare-based-border-patrol-officer-sexually-abused-robbed-women-in-2022-indictment-claims" target="_blank" >his December<b> </b>indictment</a><b> </b>was handed up by the same grand jury<b> </b>at the center of the scandal that undermined the credibility of U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros’ office this summer.</p><p>Defense attorney Michael<b> </b>Clancy<b> </b>even told U.S. District Judge<b> </b>Jorge<b> </b>Alonso<b> </b>that<b> </b>the prosecutor directly accused of misconduct, Assistant U.S. Attorney Sheri<b> </b>Mecklenburg, should be forced to testify under oath — even though she was not involved in Uribe’s case.</p><p>Alonso on Wednesday handed down a four-page<b> </b>order, in which he declined<b> </b>to dismiss the indictment leveled against Uribe. He did so after agreeing to review grand jury minutes<b> </b>from Uribe’s case. He did not directly address Clancy’s request for a hearing.</p><p>“Uribe has failed to provide any evidence that the inappropriate conduct in the Broadview Six [case] prejudiced the grand jury or in any way influenced the grand jury with regard to this case,” Alonso wrote.</p><p>Federal prosecutors say Uribe committed multiple “gunpoint sexual assaults” of four women in Schaumburg and Naperville between February and October 2022. He’s set to go to trial Tuesday.</p><p>Clancy had argued that Mecklenburg’s alleged misconduct ahead of Uribe’s indictment<b> </b><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago/2026/08/24/luis-uribe-customs-cbp-broadview-six" target="_blank" >left the grand jury “hopelessly tainted.”</a><b> </b>He also complained that <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/26/defense-attorney-wants-broadview-6-prosecutor-on-the-stand-in-cbp-sex-assault-case-she-hasnt-testified" target="_blank" >Mecklenburg still hasn’t been forced to testify</a> about what happened.</p><p>“We don’t even know the level of inappropriate statements that were made to this grand jury by [Mecklenburg],” Clancy said<b> </b>last week. “We have no idea. Because she hasn’t testified. It hasn’t been disclosed.”</p><p>Mecklenburg has been <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/27/broadview-six-boutros-chicago" target="_blank" >accused of three types of misconduct</a> before the grand jury that indicted the group of Operation Midway Blitz protesters known as the “Broadview Six.” She allegedly spoke to grand jurors outside the grand jury room and excused panel members who didn’t agree with the feds’ case.</p><p>She’s also accused of “vouching,” a forbidden practice in which prosecutors put their personal credibility on the line to support criminal charges.</p><p>U.S. District Judge April Perry presides over the “Broadview Six” case<b> </b>and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/17/broadview-six-judge-april-perry-trump-vance" target="_blank" >has yet to rule</a> on a request for sanctions or a special counsel who could investigate Boutros and others. Defense attorneys are due to file their final brief on the matter Sept. 15.</p><p>Indicted former Loretto Hospital executive<b> </b>Anosh<b> </b>Ahmed, who returned to the United States last week to face criminal charges here, also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/31/loretto-hospital-anosh-ahmed-broadview" target="_blank" >threatened to raise the issue</a>. Mecklenburg once handled his prosecution.</p><p>Alonso’s order addressed questions raised by Uribe<b> </b>about interpretation issues during grand jury testimony in his case. Clancy has said that, at some point, prosecutors decided an interpreter’s translation was inaccurate.</p><p>The judge wrote that the issue was made known<b> </b>to grand jurors<b> </b>in real time, and that the feds obtained an audio recording<b> </b>and created an updated transcript with help from<b> </b>a different interpreter. An FBI agent later summarized<b> </b>the testimony<b> </b>based on the updated transcript, Alonso explained.</p><p>“There was no misconduct,” Alonso wrote. “To the contrary, the translation issue shows that the assigned [prosecutor] acted diligently to provide the grand jury with accurate information.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2025/12/09/ohare-based-border-patrol-officer-sexually-abused-robbed-women-in-2022-indictment-claims" target="_blank" >O’Hare-based Border Protection officer sexually abused, robbed women at gunpoint, indictment claims</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago/2026/08/24/luis-uribe-customs-cbp-broadview-six" target="_blank" >CBP agent says feds’ ‘Broadview Six’ misconduct tainted his sexual assault case</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/26/defense-attorney-wants-broadview-6-prosecutor-on-the-stand-in-cbp-sex-assault-case-she-hasnt-testified" target="_blank" >Defense attorney wants ‘Broadview 6' prosecutor on the stand in CBP sex assault case: ‘She hasn’t testified’</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Rookie DT Jordan van den Berg is raw — but exactly what the Bears need
entries.summary: <p>Like a barnstorming wrestler, all <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> rookie defensive tackle Jordan van den Berg needs is a finishing move. He has to develop a reliable way to shed a run-blocker and get past a pass-blocker.</p><p>Until then, though, the sixth-round pick will keep doing what earned him a roster spot and enabled the Bears to trade Gervon Dexter to the Falcons — use his otherworldly athleticism to sew chaos.</p><p>“A lot of times with defensive linemen, you can have a lot of hidden production where you’re just so disruptive that you create opportunities for other players,” Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said Wednesday.  “And that’s probably where he’s at right now.”</p><p>Allen has delighted in it. This offseason, Allen decided he wanted his defensive line to get more explosive and play with more effort. Those traits are what made the 24-year-old South African the defensive star of training camp.</p><p>Case in point: In the third quarter of the Bears’ second preseason game, the 6-foot-3, 310-pound van den Berg leapt like Superman to try to tackle Bengals quarterback Sean Clifford as he scrambled out of bounds. He missed — but he went viral. His coaches noticed, too.</p><p>“They were proud of the effort …" van den Berg said. "I just try to attack every play with as much energy and passion as I can.”</p><p>He's been exactly what the Bears needed. The Bears know the risks of leaning on the raw van den Berg as part of a defensive tackle rotation that includes likely starters Grady Jarrett and Kentavius Street as well as Neville Gallimore, who are all veterans. But they also know the upside that comes with it.</p><p>They drafted van den Berg because his athleticism was off the charts. They needed to find out whether he could play. The answer, at least through the preseason, is a resounding yes. Pro Football Focus ranked him 17<sup>th</sup> out of the 154 defensive tackles they graded during preseason games this year.</p><p>“He’s got all the skillset, he’s got the physicality, he’s got the effort,” Allen said.</p><p>Not bad for someone who wasn’t even invited to the NFL Scouting Combine.</p><p>Born in Johannesburg, van den Berg moved to the Atlanta area at 10. A linebacker in high school — and a zero-star prospect — he went to Iowa Western Community College, where he gained 40 pounds and switched to defensive line. From there he transferred to Penn State, where he played sparingly, and later back home to Georgia Tech.</p><p>“He took the long road,” Bears national scout Brendan Rehor said.</p><p>He brought his loud tools with him. Relative Athletic Score is a rubric that measures the size, explosion, speed and agility of every NFL prospect. He scored a perfect 10.</p><p>There have been 2,098 defensive tackles measured since 1987. He has the second-best RAS ever recorded at the position — behind only the Eagles’ Jordan Davis, a first-round pick who signed a three-year, $78 million extension in March.</p><p>Athleticism runs in the family. His grandpa competed in Mr. Universe competitions and his grandma held South African swimming records.</p><p>“He has a mean streak,” defensive line coach Jeremy Garrett said. “He can bend, he can run. … Now it's just honing it in to where he's not so out of control.”</p><p>It’s a lot easier for coaches to have players dial their motors down than up. That’s why Johnson had to remind him, with a smile, not to hit the quarterback when he’s out of bounds.</p><p>“I’m still learning technique,” van den Berg said. “Trying to work on fundamentals.”</p><p>The rookie has been leaning on Bears veterans for tips, saying that his "development of the game — and my understanding through them — has just completely changed." His position coach at Georgia Tech, Jess Simpson, made his players watch tape of Jarrett every day. Now van den Berg has the chance to pick his brain up close.</p><p>“He's hungry to learn,” Jarrett said. “Hungry to work.”</p><p></p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module entries.title: Bears' practice report: It's a scorcher out there!
entries.summary: <p>Breaking down <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a>’ Wednesday training camp practice with the Titans:</p><h3><b>What happened</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The team went over an hour as the temperature hit 94 degrees, and the players got frequent two-minute water breaks because of the heat. That weather could be similar to what they encounter next Sunday against the Panthers. The offense worked mainly on various scenarios where they were trailing late in the game.</p><h3><b>New guy</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Cornerback Clark Phillips wasn’t expecting the Falcons to trade him, but they sent him to the Bears as part of the Gervon Dexter trade Sunday. “It’s definitely a unique thing,” he said of changing teams so close to the start of the season. “But I’m prepared for it. I’m excited to be here.” The Bears are testing whether he can help them at nickel cornerback, or if he’s going to be exclusively on the outside.</p><h3><b>Lineup forming</b></h3><h3></h3><p>All indications point toward the Bears going with veteran Kentavius Street, whom defensive coordinator Dennis Allen called “the most-productive tackle we had throughout the course of training camp,” in place of Gervon Dexter. Rookie Malik Muhammad is in line to start at nickel cornerback for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/01/bears-gm-ryan-poles-kyler-gordon-do-not-know-play-again-calf-injury-nfl-slot-cornerback" >Kyler Gordon</a>, and Xavier Woods at safety for Coby Bryant.</p><h3><b>Injury updates</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The Bears were mostly healthy: Only running back Kyle Monangai, defensive end Austin Booker and linebacker D’Marco Jackson were out. Defensive end Marcus Davenport, on the practice squad, exited after individual drills. Cornerback Jaylon Johnson (elbow) was full-go.</p><h3><b>What’s next?</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The Bears will hold their final preseason practice Thursday, then give players a long weekend to refresh.</p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-show-loadmore="true" ><a class="AnchorLink" entries.title: Notre Dame RB Aneyas Williams ready to make long-awaited 1st start as No. 4 Irish face Wisconsin
entries.summary: <p>SOUTH BEND, Ind. — Notre Dame running back Aneyas Williams spent his first two college seasons waiting for a chance to prove himself. Then last winter, he had right elbow surgery and considered transferring.</p><p>Eventually, Williams decided to come back to South Bend to show he could replace not one, but two NFL first-round draft picks.</p><p>On Sunday, Williams is expected to make his long-awaited first college start when the No. 4 Fighting Irish face Wisconsin at historic Lambeau Field, and it's starting to feel more like what Williams envisioned when he chose Notre Dame.</p><p>"I didn't feel right," he said when asked about changing schools. "I came here for a reason. This degree means something to me, but also these people mean something more to me."</p><p>He added: "With (Jadarian Price and Jeremiyah Love) gone, obviously the opportunity is there. We're looking to replace these guys. We're not looking to take any steps back at all in the running back room."</p><p>It certainly hasn't been the journey most top-ranked recruits map out.</p><p>The prep star from Hannibal, Missouri, watched Love hurdle his way into Heisman Trophy contention, and along with Price, field one of the top running duos in Notre Dame's storied history. They led the Irish to the national championship game in January 2025 and were good enough to keep Notre Dame in playoff contention after last season's 0-2 start on their way to becoming the first running back tandem from the same school to be selected in the first round of the NFL draft since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger.</p><p>But playing behind those two meant Williams was essentially relegated to spot or mop-up duty, and in today's college transfer environment that means other schools can offer more money, more playing time or both.</p><p>Williams called the experience "exciting" though the chance to team up with incumbent starting quarterback CJ Carr as the cornerstones of Notre Dame's offense was even more enticing.</p><p>"I want (people) to see the player that I can and have been," he said. "You know, since I've been here, I might have taken a back seat, but I learned a lot in those years. Now, to just apply it and bring it to the field, and give these younger guys someone to look up to like I had, that's the biggest thing."</p><p>Williams showed his potential in 2024, playing in 13 games, rushing for 219 yards and logging another 172 yards receiving. Last year, the 5-foot-10, 210-pound Williams appeared in all 12 games but had just 24 carries for 224 yards and finished with five TDs.</p><p>His biggest game came in Notre Dame's season finale when he rushed 10 times for 83 yards, caught two passes for 40 yards and scored twice including a 51-yard TD run in 49-20 rout over Stanford. When the Irish were left out of the 12-team playoff, the team elected not to appear in a bowl game.</p><p>Williams knows the outside world remains skeptical of what Notre Dame's offense will look like without Love and Price, though he dismisses any suggestion the Irish runners can't get the job done.</p><p>"I'd be silly to say I don't hear it," he said. "I've seen a lot about how the running back room is going to be the weak spot, and I think you take that and use it. I think that's the message that we've used in the running back room, and (running backs coach Ja'Juan Seider) has put on us."</p><p>And Seider has no doubt Williams has always had what it takes.</p><p>"He has a know-how of what's going on around him," Seider said, noting Williams was one of last season's leaders. "He knows the big picture. He's very similar to what CJ has as a quarterback. He can see the rotation of the safety. He can see the front change, and he can anticipate, which to me, that is what makes a great running back, to be able anticipate what's going on around him and evade."<br></p>

entries.title: Tiger Woods pleads no contest to reckless driving charge
entries.summary: <p>STUART, Florida — Tiger Woods pleaded no contest to a reckless driving charge and his driver's license was suspended for five years Wednesday following a March rollover crash in Florida, where he initially was accused of driving under the influence.</p><p>Woods, still one of golf's most influential figures and as recognizable as any athlete in the world, has had a remarkable fall since winning the 2019 Masters for his 15th major. The first person of Black heritage to win the Masters in 1997, his career has been derailed by multiple back and knee surgeries, car crashes and dependence on pain medication.</p><p>He was arrested in March after his SUV clipped a truck and rolled over on its side on a beachside residential road near his home on Jupiter Island. A sheriff's report said deputies found two pain pills in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment. He did a Breathalyzer test, which came out negative, but refused to take a urine test.</p><p>He pleaded not guilty to the original DUI charge.</p><p>Before the hearing in Florida's Marin County on Wednesday, Woods, 50, sat at the defense table looking back at the mostly empty courtroom gallery. He said little as he agreed to the reduced charge and left the courthouse without addressing reporters.</p><p>He had arrived with his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, President Donald Trump's former daughter-in-law. She sat behind him during the proceedings.</p><p>"Tiger is not absolved of accountability and he surrendered his license for the next five years," Mark Steinberg, his longtime manager at Excel Sports told the AP. "He is continuing his treatment and prioritizing all aspects of his health."</p><h3>Prosecutor says Tiger Woods has a tolerance to pain medicine</h3><p>The prosecutor in the case said two toxicologists found there was insufficient proof of his impairment and determined Woods had built up a "pharmacological" tolerance after years of using pain pills.</p><p>Thomas Bakkedahl, a state attorney, defended his decision to accept the plea, saying, "I did what I think is right."</p><p>Prosecutors obtained the golfer's pharmacy records that showed he had a lawful prescription, Bakkedahl said.</p><p>The deputy who arrested Woods after the crash found two white pills in his pocket that had markings identifying them as hydrocodone, according to the arrest report. Hydrocodone is an opioid that is prescribed for pain, but it can be addictive.</p><p>Woods told the deputy he takes a few prescription medications, according to the report, including "Vicodin" — a brand name painkiller that contains hydrocodone.</p><p>He has had numerous surgeries on his legs and back over the last two decades — some to treat cartilage and ligament damage, a ruptured tendon, arthritis, and damaged discs in his back.</p><p>At Wednesday's hearing, Woods also pleaded no contest to refusing to submit to testing after the crash and was fined $1,500, according to court documents. A no-contest plea is not an admission of guilt, but means the accused will offer no defense. The plea is treated as a conviction in the criminal justice system.</p><p>Woods' attorney did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.</p><h3>Video shows the aftermath of the crash</h3><p>Body camera footage shows Woods taking out his phone after the crash and telling a deputy, "I was just talking to the president."</p><p>Woods can be heard saying, "Thank you so much," as he hangs up and the deputy approaches. It is not clear if Woods was referring to President Donald Trump.</p><p>The footage also shows the handcuffed Woods hiccupping, yawning and repeatedly appearing to nod off during the 15-minute ride.</p><p>Neither Woods nor the person in the other vehicle were injured in the crash, according to officials. Woods told a deputy that he was looking down at his phone and changing the radio station when he hit the truck.</p><p>Woods has been involved in four crashes over the years. He took a leave from the golf tour after the 2009 crash and again after the latest crash and has yet to return to tournament play.</p><p>He left the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient treatment facility, according to court records.</p><p>Woods made his first public appearance since returning from treatment on June 23 when he introduced the PGA Tour's plans to revamp its schedule for 2028. Woods remained as chair of the tour's Future Competition Committee after his arrest.</p><h3>It’s not clear if Tiger is allowed to drive a golf cart</h3><p>Judge Darren Steele warned Woods that his driver's license suspension didn't include any exceptions.</p><p>"If you were to drive for any reason at all, you would immediately go back to jail," the judge told Woods.</p><p>The prosecutor said he was confident that Woods would be spotted if he doesn't heed the message.</p><p>"Of all the people in the world who should not get behind the wheel of a car, it's one of the most recognizable people on the planet," Bakkedahl said.</p><p>But what wasn't immediately clear is whether Woods can drive a golf cart on a golf course. Bakkedahl told reporters he needed to check on that.<br></p>

entries.title: Back-to-back bond rating upgrades for Illinois boost Pritzker's reelection bid
entries.summary: <p>Illinois just received a new financial accolade from a top bond rating agency, giving Gov. JB Pritzker a strategic boost in a fall campaign where Republican challenger Darren Bailey has made the state’s fiscal management under Pritzker a central issue.</p><p>S&P Global Ratings <a class="Link" href="https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/sourceId/101704763" target="_blank" ><u>raised </u></a>Illinois' general obligation bond rating from an “A-” to an “A,” marking the 12th bond rating upgrade for the state since Pritzker took office in 2019.</p><p>S&P cited the passage of consecutive balanced state budgets and the “ongoing build-up of operating reserves” in the event of an economic recession since the last credit upgrade in February 2023. The agency said Illinois’ fiscal outlook is “stable.”</p><p>Last week, Moody’s Investors Service upgraded its own bond rating for Illinois, saying the state has demonstrated “conservative fiscal management.”</p><p>In a statement, Pritzker said the back-to-back upgrades show Illinois’ financial progress is built to last, “even as the Trump Administration creates uncertainty and new challenges.”</p><p>Last week, the two-term governor made a campaign stop in Springfield on a statewide bus tour and rubbed the nose of Abraham Lincoln’s bronze bust outside the tomb in which he’s buried. The governor’s office said Pritzker, who is seeking a third term, was hoping for good luck and for another credit upgrade.</p><p>“Working alongside the General Assembly, we have transformed Illinois from a state defined by fiscal instability into one earning recognition for responsible financial management,” Pritzker said.</p><p>A higher bond rating usually means lower borrowing costs for the state. The two credit upgrades come as the state prepares to sell general obligation bonds later this month. According to Pritzker’s office, proceeds from the sale will go toward infrastructure projects and the state’s pension buyout program for state and university employees, as well as public school teachers outside of Chicago.</p><p>The rosier assessment of the state’s finances forced Bailey on Wednesday to at least partly soften some of his earlier attacks on Pritzker’s financial stewardship of Illinois through nearly two terms in office.</p><p>“Illinois getting a credit upgrade is good news,” Bailey said in a Facebook post. “I’m not going to tell you otherwise just because I’m running against JB Pritzker.”</p><p>Despite making that acknowledgment, Bailey continued to point the finger at Pritzker for making the state less affordable through high property, sales and gas taxes.</p><p>“He made YOU pay more to afford government,” Bailey wrote. “More at the pump. More at the toll booth. More to register your car. A lot more when the property tax bill comes. Death by a thousand cuts. And Illinois families are bleeding out.”</p><p>Bailey also said Illinois still has the lowest credit rating of any state in the U.S., which is backed up by a recent S&P Global <a class="Link" href="https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/us-state-ratings-and-outlooks-current-list-s2023750" target="_blank" ><u>report</u></a> ranking states by credit ranking. The list shows Illinois is the only state with a single “A” grade, behind Kentucky which has earned an “A+.”</p><p>“So yes, I’m glad Illinois can borrow money cheaper,” Bailey said. “Now let’s make Illinois cheaper to live in.”</p><p>Moody’s <a class="Link" href="https://ratings.moodys.com/ratings-news/471726" target="_blank" ><u>points </u></a>to Illinois’ long-standing pension funding crisis and amendments in the state constitution that prohibit a more progressive tax structure as reasons why Illinois is an outlier among other states. But according to Pritzker, former Republican Gov. Bruce Rauner should shoulder much of the blame for causing a two-year budget impasse.</p><p>“Before Governor Pritzker took office, Illinois endured 24 credit rating downgrades over 15 years, including eight downgrades between 2015 and 2017,” Pritzker's office said in a statement, citing the time frame when Rauner was in office. “The state accumulated nearly $17 billion in unpaid bills, depleted its financial reserves, and went more than two decades without receiving a credit rating upgrade.”</p><p>The general election will take place Nov. 3.</p>

entries.title: White Sox activate Davis Martin from injured list ahead of his Wednesday night start against the Astros
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON — Davis Martin is scheduled to start the third game of a four-game set against the Astros, so the White Sox had just the small bit of housekeeping of actually adding him to the roster.</p><p>Martin was officially activated from the injured list on Wednesday afternoon, after missing roughly three weeks for a blister on his middle finger. Prospect right-hander Tanner McDougal, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/01/white-sox-prospect-tanner-mcdougal-looking-to-show-improved-mechanics-after-rocky-debut-colson-montgomery-davis-martin-will-venable" target="_blank" ><u>still in the throes of mechanical adjustments to his delivery</u></a>, was optioned back to Triple-A Charlotte after a single day on the active roster. McDougal did not pitch in Tuesday’s 5-1 victory in Houston.</p><p>For the first two months of 2026, the 29-year-old Martin pitched to a 2.00 ERA with a 27% strikeout rate and looked bound for the All-Star Game. Since June 1, he has a 7.06 ERA and is striking out just 15% of hitters. His last start in the majors saw Martin allow four runs (three earned) and two homers in just two innings against the light-hitting Cincinnati Reds, before being ejected for a wildly misfired pitch that clipped first baseman Sal Stewart in the helmet.</p><p>"I’m really confident I’m going to find it and I’m going to be a key piece down the stretch," Martin said after that game.</p><p>Now, Martin is coming off an efficient five innings of scoreless baseball in his lone Triple-A rehab start last week, in which he allowed just two baserunners and struck out five. Martin has been traveling with the team in anticipation of his return to the rotation, and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/28/davis-martin-return-il-first-half-white-sox-pitchers" target="_blank" ><u>expressed confidence</u></a> he was able to use his time off as a mechanical and mental reset.</p><p>The White Sox rotation sorely needs a refurbished version of Martin. With Sean Burke getting pulled after a career-high 104 pitches in 5⅔ scoreless innings in Tuesday’s 5-1 victory, the Sox have not enjoyed a quality start (six innings or more, three earned runs or less) since Anthony Kay in their Aug. 20 loss to the Braves.</p><p></p><p></p><p></p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Suspect arrested in Chinatown bank robbery attempt
entries.summary: <p>A quick attempt at robbing a bank in Chinatown Wednesday morning led to a quick grab of the suspect, the FBI said. </p><p>The robbery attempt happened at 10:40 a.m. at the U.S. Bank branch in the 2100 block of South China Place, according to an FBI spokesperson, who said there was a "quick attempt and quick grab."</p><p>No physical injuries were reported, though such crimes can take a mental toll on bank staffers, the spokesperson said.</p><p>The FBI provided no information on the person in custody.<br></p>

entries.title: Mom of Faceworld gang member found guilty of retaliating against a witness in son's murder case
entries.summary: <p>Donnita Bryant wasn’t accused of pulling a trigger, taking part in a kidnapping or committing any of the other brutal crimes federal prosecutors have tied to the South Side street gang known as Faceworld.</p><p>But prosecutors say the mother of convicted Faceworld killer Diontae Harper joined her son's campaign of intimidation and helped post a videotaped law enforcement interview on social media to brand a government witness a “rat.”</p><p>On Wednesday, a jury found Bryant and a Faceworld associate guilty of conspiring with Harper to retaliate against witnesses in his murder case — the latest development in a sprawling FBI crackdown that's swept up at least a dozen reputed Faceworld members over the past three years.</p><div class="Enhancement" photo</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Earlier this year, Harper pleaded guilty to a federal charge that accused him of firing into a car at a South Side gas station and killing a 22-year-old man in 2020. He also pleaded guilty on Aug. 17 to the charges in the witness retaliation case.</p><p>Bryant, who was a Chicago Transit Authority employee, was charged in the witness retaliation case along with Faceworld associate Markeeves Brooks and Michaela Richard, the mother of the daughter of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2021/11/17/22788277/pair-charged-killing-armored-truck-guard-fatally-shooting-accomplices-murderous-spree-south-side" target="_blank" ><u>Harper’s slain brother Naiqwon</u></a>.</p><p>On Wednesday, the jury convicted Brooks but acquitted Richard.</p><p>Richard, a teacher's aide in Bronzeville, was worried a felony conviction would scuttle her dream career as a teacher, said her lawyer, Christopher Grohman. </p><p>“She will be a productive citizen," Grohman said. "She's one of my favorite clients of all time. She's ecstatic the jury was able to parse out the evidence.”</p><p>The trio were accused of arranging a social media post of a witness interview conducted by an FBI agent and a Chicago police detective in Harper's murder case. The interview was uploaded on Instagram to an account with tens of thousands of followers, many of whom responded with comments such as "rat, rat, rat, want some cheese?"</p><p>The aim of the post, according to prosecutors, was to put a target on the back of the witness. In Chicago's gang world, witnesses are sometimes killed for cooperating with the government.</p><p>"Donnita Bryant was eyes wide open that what they were doing was wrong," Assistant U.S. Attorney Jessica Ecker told jurors in her closing argument after a six-day trial.</p><p>But defense attorneys said the motive was innocent — to show that Harper wasn't a rat and clear his name.</p><p>"It's not a crime to stick up for your son," William Stanton, one of Bryant's lawyers, told jurors.</p><p>The case offered a window into the violence prosecutors say Faceworld unleashed on West Chatham and surrounding South Side neighborhoods — more than a dozen killings, the gang rape of a woman forced to drink bleach and Harper's behind-bars campaign to expose government witnesses.</p><p>Faceworld, a faction of the Gangster Disciples, was named for a teen named Cornell “King Face” Henderson, who was shot to death in 2010. More than a decade later, prosecutors say, the gang was wreaking havoc across the South Side and suburbs, including Harper’s involvement in the May, 13, 2020, killing of Paul Harris at a GoLo gas station near 89th and Halsted streets. The gang has even been accused of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2019/7/29/8937962/two-women-killed-mothers-against-senseless-killings-gresham-chicago-gun-violence" involving government witnesses to his family. </p><p>Harper, an acknowledged Faceworld member, pleaded guilty in January 2025 to killing Harris. While in the Metropolitan Correctional Center, he got his hands on a protected 2023 grand jury transcript containing testimony from Keshawn “Flup” Wordlow, one of the witnesses against him and others in the gang. </p><p>But jail officials intercepted the transcript in the mail in April 2025, prosecutors said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-floatLeft> <div class="Enhancement-item" Committee</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>The next month, Harper was sentenced to 34 years in prison in the Harris murder case. U.S. District Judge Manish Shah told Harper that he failed to accept a basic rule of civilization: “Don’t kill.” The judge also said he’d considered Harper's unsuccessful plot to mail out the transcript an “aggravating factor” in his sentence.</p><p>Harper, who originally faced the possibility of the death penalty, struck a contrite note in court.</p><p>“I was definitely caught up in the moment, in the lifestyle, in a way of living that made me feel and do wrong things, gain short-sighted benefits that only spiraled into more wrong things and more violence,” he said.</p><p>But prosecutors say that within weeks Harper was at it again — this time targeting another witness, Amonti McClure. Harper had approached McClure in jail and warned him he was in danger for testifying against the gang. On a recorded call, Harper said McClure and Wordlow were “gonna get stabbed.”</p><p>After his sentencing, Harper called his mom and told her that he planned to obtain McClure’s videotaped interview with the FBI and police. Harper then mailed out a CD of the recording.</p><p>Bryant, 47, Richard, 26, and Brooks, 29, were accused of working to get the footage to social media sites that focus on gangs.</p><p>"Now that he took 34 years, I'm gonna let the cat out of the bag," Bryant said in one text message. </p><p>She told Richard: "They will see snitching not in our blood."</p><div class="Enhancement" The next month, the interview was posted on Instagram on the Live With Baba TV account, which had more than 57,000 followers.</p><p>After his first attempt at mailing out Wordlow's grand jury testimony failed, Harper was able to mail another copy to family members by putting a phony "attorney" label on the envelope to keep jail officials from intercepting it. But the contents of that transcript were never posted on social media, prosecutors said.</p><p>Defense attorneys stressed that while Harper wasn’t supposed to disseminate the grand jury transcript and the recorded interview because of protective orders, Bryant, Brooks and Richard weren’t bound by them.</p><p>The defense attorneys also noted that Bryant and Richard were cooperative with the FBI during a September 2025 search of Bryant’s home. They pointed out that FBI agents failed to take the copy of the McClure interview video during the raid, but Richard called them and they came back and got it.</p><p>Grohman, a former prosecutor with about 25 trials under his belt, said he's never seen anything like that. He said it showed his client, Richard, "didn't think she was doing anything criminal."</p><p>The defense attorneys said the impact of the video being posted on Instagram was minimal, especially because McClure's and Wordlow’s cooperation was already disclosed in court records that anyone could see.</p><p>"His nickname already is 'The Police,'" said Lisa Marie Noller, one of Brooks' lawyers.</p><p>Defense attorneys added that McClure was never physically harmed because of the video. And they said none of the defendants — Bryant, Richard or Brooks — mentioned a desire to physically harm either witness in their phone calls and texts.</p><p>But prosecutors said McClure felt like he was in “survival mode” with a “target on his back” and was having a difficult time sleeping. They said the goal of posting the video of the interview was retaliation — not clearing Harper’s name. And the danger was very real, they say. </p><p>In a case involving the Hobos, another violent gang on the South Side, federal prosecutors accused members of <a class="Link" entries.title: Big Ten Network set to begin 20th season with its original cast
entries.summary: <p>When Big Ten Network’s football pregame show hits the air at 4:30 p.m. Thursday, it will feature the same trio that appeared when the network launched on Aug. 30, 2007.</p><p>Host Dave Revsine and analysts Gerry DiNardo and Howard Griffith aren’t always in the studio together these days, but they will come together before an opening-night doubleheader, capped by UAB-Illinois, to commemorate BTN’s 20th season.</p><p>“It’s really special to be working with them tomorrow night,” Revsine said Wednesday. “I think we’ll do a little bit of a nod to our history together. One of the things that we’re really trying to do with this is not make it about us. But I can’t think of many scenarios in the sports-television world where you have three guys who have been together that whole time.”</p><p>BTN will celebrate its anniversary with special programming in the fall. “B1G Network Season 20: 20 Moments” will show fans the most memorable moments that aired on the network. “The B1G Story: Rise of Women’s Sports” will examine how the conference helped lead the movement. “B1G Network Season 20: Moments and Memories” will bring Revsine, DiNardo and Griffith together with fellow originals Rick Pizzo and Mike Hall to discuss the network’s origin.</p><p>Revsine has been the face of the network from the start. The irony is that when he first met with BTN officials about the job, he only did it to give himself leverage with his then-employer, ESPN, as he sought a new contract. Revsine had spent more than a decade there as an anchor and play-by-play voice.</p><p>But after meeting with original BTN executive producer Leon Schweir, Revsine became intrigued. Then he realized the network wasn’t talking to anyone else about the job. After returning to have dinner with then-BTN president Mark Silverman and Big Ten commissioner Jim Delany, Revsine was sold.</p><p>“I remember my thought was, I’m going where they’re going,” he said.</p><p>But not everyone was sold, particularly at ESPN, which wanted Revsine to stay.</p><p>“All these people were coming up to me, like, ‘Are you sure you know what you’re doing?’ ” Revsine said. “ ‘You’re in a good spot here. Why would you do this?’ I had no hesitation.</p><p>“I was convinced this was the right thing for me. I just didn’t know how good. I don’t think that I envisioned that it would be as great as it’s been and that it would change college-sports television in the way that it has.”</p><p>Eventually, ESPN launched the SEC Network, then the ACC Network. The Pac-12 launched a network on its own, and that decision plus distribution issues led to its demise. BTN has had its share of carriage disputes, including at launch, when it wasn’t available on Comcast cable. Now, with members from coast to coast, it’s carried by every major distributor in the country.</p><p>Revsine said he notices the network’s reach everywhere he goes. While out to dinner with his wife and another couple in Chicago, about a week after visiting Iowa on BTN's training-camp tour, Revsine said a Hawkeyes fan approached him to talk about the team’s quarterbacks, who had had a rough practice the day of Revsine's visit.</p><p>”I don’t think I really understood how connected we were going feel to the schools and by extension to the fans,” Revsine said. “You have people come up to you and start talking to you, address you by name as if you’re old friends, and just talk about their team. That part of it is really neat.”</p><p>So is being able to work with the same people for 20 seasons.</p><p>“It speaks to what a great place it has been to work,” Revsine said.</p><div entries.title: Video emerges of Kyler Gordon workout 1 day after Bears cast doubt on return
entries.summary: <p>One day after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> general manager Ryan Poles said he couldn’t guarantee that slot cornerback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/halas-intrigue/2026/09/01/bears-kyler-gordon-podcast-halas-intrigue" target="_blank" >Kyler Gordon</a> would ever play for them again, a rehab specialist posted videos of Gordon going through private workouts.</p><p>The “Foot Doctor Moe” Instagram account — linked to Montel Fleming, a rehab specialist — <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/stories/footdoctor_moe/ " target="_blank" >posted clips of Gordon</a>, wearing Bears shorts and a baggy T-shirt, doing lunges, jumping and sprinting. It’s unclear when the videos were shot — it wasn't at Halas Hall — but the messaging is clear. Gordon was moving fairly well.</p><p>Captions written beneath the video includes “Priming the right way” and saying that “how you really fix an injury” is understanding where in the body the issue is.</p><p>In the past, Fleming has has posted videos of work he’s done with Bears D’Andre Swift, Jaylon Johnson and Cam Lewis.</p><p>Gordon has been out with a calf injury since the spring. Poles said Tuesday that he didn’t know if Gordon would play for the Bears again, but said he was hopeful. He and Bears coach Ben Johnson have been openly frustrated with his slow recovery.</p><p>“I think when people come back from injuries, there's different things that happen,” Poles said. “Sometimes they return fast, sometimes they're slow. So it's really a timing thing and healing thing and confidence thing.”<br></p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Craig Counsell’s reunion with ex-Brewer Tyrone Taylor fruitful for Cubs: ‘I knew he’d fit in really well’
entries.summary: <p>Craig Counsell had a request for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> president Jed Hoyer at the trade deadline.</p><p>He wanted a right-handed hitting outfielder to bring off the bench.</p><p>Hoyer was focused on adding pitching, and he did, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-jed-hoyer-top-prospects-trades-kevin-gausman-clay-holmes-ryan-zeferjahn-braxton-garrett-tyrone-taylor" >bringing in righties Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes</a> to slot at the top of the Cubs’ starting rotation.</p><p>But Counsell had a suggested name, too, a guy he managed for parts of five seasons in Milwaukee.</p><p>How about Tyrone Taylor?</p><p>“That was a spot on the roster that he was focused on,” Hoyer said Tuesday. “Taylor was a guy he brought up. As he was thinking about how to use the bench and the lineup at the end of the year, that kind of player would fit really well for us.”</p><p>The Cubs landed Taylor in the same deal with the Mets that netted Holmes and envisioned the outfielder as a role player who could contribute offensively and defensively, good enough with the glove to give <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/30/chicago-cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-mvp-wins-above-replacement-home-runs-craig-counsell-ryan-flaherty-john-mallee-cincinnati-reds" >MVP candidate</a> Pete Crow-Armstrong breaks in center field, if needed.</p><p>It turns out he’s someone they maybe didn’t know how much they needed.</p><p>Taylor’s been excellent at the plate, bringing a 1.027 OPS as a Cub into Wednesday’s game against his former team.</p><p>“Let’s say I didn’t know him, his general skill set fit us really well,” Counsell said Wednesday. “I know Tyrone. I knew he’d fit in really well here, and he has.</p><p>“He’s always been like, ‘I know what my job is. I’m going to do that job well.’ Simple as that. Nothing more than that.</p><p>“He was a really good high-school football player. He kind of competes like a football player sometimes, a little bit, and that’s always a good thing.”</p><p>So not a bad recommendation from the skipper, huh?</p><p>“1.000 OPS, right?” Hoyer said. “That’s not that subtle.”</p><p>Counsell’s known Taylor for a long time, known that he’s been someone his teams, be they Brewers or Cubs, could always benefit from.</p><p>But did he know he could do this?</p><p>“I can remember seeing him on a backfield when he was 18 years old, and I don’t know that I would have thought that he would turn into this type of hitter,” Counsell said. “He was more like a contact, ‘spray the ball around the field’ type guy. And he’s turned into a guy who can hit home runs.</p><p>“But he was a really good competitor and a really good athlete, and those things always work.”</p><p>Taylor’s on the other side of the Cubs-Brewers rivalry now, making his presence felt in the first two games of this week’s series, starting the scoring in a 17-3 blowout Monday with a first-inning home run – the first of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/31/cubs-brewers-jed-hoyer-trades-free-agency-alex-bregman-clay-holmes-tyrone-taylor" >the team’s record nine long balls</a> – and doubling home half his team’s runs in Tuesday’s 9-4 loss.</p><p>Taylor came into Wednesday with a pair of four-hit games on the home stand and four multi-hit efforts in his previous eight contests.</p><p>But this isn’t a one-way compliment street.</p><p>Taylor had high praise for his former and current manager, too, seeing Counsell’s presence as part of what makes the Cubs a potentially dangerous team come October.</p><p>“He’s really good at putting his guys in good positions to succeed,” Taylor said. “He’s played before, too, so he understands the everyday grind of it. He’s very intelligent when it comes to the baseball rules and stuff.</p><p>“I think he’s one of the best managers. I guess he got paid like one, too. It makes sense.”</p><p>The big-money investment in luring Counsell south of the state line is an integral part of the Cubs-Brewers story – as is the fact that <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/31/brewers-own-cubs-rivalry-milwaukee-chicago-pat-murphy-craig-counsell-wrigley-field-mlb" >the Brewers have kept besting the Cubs</a> in the division race since he switched sides.</p><p>It looks increasingly unlikely that the Brewers, who started Wednesday with an eight-game lead in the NL Central standings, will be dethroned this season. But come playoff time? Could the Cubs get revenge on their postseason ousters from a year ago?</p><p>“We’ve got the talent in here to go all the way,” Taylor said, “but also, we know it’s important to take it day by day and one game at a time.”</p><p>Yeah, that fits Counsell’s Cubs perfectly.</p>
entries.author: Vinnie Duber

entries.title: NBA fines Clippers and Kawhi Leonard, suspends owner Steve Ballmer one year in cap circumvention case
entries.summary: <p>LOS ANGELES — Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for one year by the NBA, and the team was ordered to forfeit five first-round draft picks and pay a $30 million fine Wednesday for violating salary cap circumvention rules in a case involving Kawhi Leonard.</p><p>Also, president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank has been banned for six months and team president of business operations Gillian Zucker was suspended for one year. Leonard was hit with a $700,000 penalty.</p><p>The league came down hard on the organization after a nearly year-long investigation led by an outside law firm.</p><p>The Clippers had said multiple times that they had done nothing wrong and expected to be exonerated.</p><p>The team maintained that stance after the league's announcement.</p><p>"We vehemently reject the NBA's findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence," the team said in a statement. "What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly, and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner (Adam) Silver set at the start of this investigation to ensure it's fairness and accuracy."</p><p>The Clippers said they will "now fight just as hard to demonstrate our innocence. We intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process."</p><p>The NBA opened the investigation in September 2025 into whether a $28 million endorsement contract between Leonard and Aspiration Fund Adviser LLC — a company that filed for bankruptcy last year — broke league rules, following a report by podcast journalist Pablo Torre. Earlier this year, Aspiration co-founder Joseph Sanberg was sentenced to 14 years in federal prison after pleading guilty to defrauding investors and lenders of at least $248 million.</p><p>"I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family," Leonard said in a statement issued through his new agent, Harrison Gaines.</p><p>The NBA said Leonard, through his former business manager and uncle Dennis Robertson, "violated the circumvention rules by pressuring the Clippers to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses."</p><p>"I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap," Leonard said in his statement.</p><p>The league said Ballmer was suspended for "knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities," among other issues.</p><p>Leonard's trade to the Toronto Raptors has been on hold pending the outcome of the investigation. The Raptors had said they still want Leonard, and he apparently is just as eager to return to the team where he won an NBA title in 2019, when he was Finals MVP.</p><p>"As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate," Leonard said in his statement.<br></p>

entries.title: Aspira permitirá que juez decida el destino del dinero de la venta de una escuela construida con fondos públicos
entries.summary: <p>Después de que Aspira de Illinois se declaró en bancarrota en junio, la organización sin fines de lucro incluyó en su lista un edificio construido con $27 millones en fondos públicos que albergaba una de sus escuelas chárter cerradas. En documentos de la corte, la organización indicó que planeaba usar el dinero de la venta para pagar deudas y continuar operando con lo que quedara.</p><p>En cambio, la semana pasada, un abogado de la organización le dijo a un juez que Aspira apartará el dinero de la venta y esperará a que la corte decida a dónde debe ir. No está claro exactamente con cuánto dinero podría quedarse Aspira. Chicago Public Schools envió a un abogado a la audiencia sobre la venta de la propiedad, lo que indica que el distrito escolar está listo para sostener que debería recibir parte, si no es que la totalidad, del dinero restante.</p><p>Estos últimos hechos en el caso de bancarrota de Aspira ocurren después de que <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/08/12/aspira-se-declara-en-bancarrota-y-podria-quedarse-con-la-venta-de-edificio-financiado-con-dinero-publico" target="_blank" >WBEZ y el Chicago Sun-Times publicaron un artículo</a> que cuestionaba si Aspira podría embolsarse dinero de la venta.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-ae0000" name="module-ae0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Lo que pase en este caso podría sentar un precedente sobre qué ocurre con los activos comprados con fondos públicos cuando operadores privados cierran escuelas chárter en Illinois. A CPS se le ha criticado por no perseguir los activos de chárter cerradas en el pasado, pero parece que el distrito escolar está interviniendo ahora.</p><p>Funcionarios de CPS dijeron en un comunicado emitido el viernes que "se abstienen de proporcionar detalles sobre procedimientos legales pendientes", pero señalaron que están llevando a cabo "los procedimientos legales apropiados para garantizar que cualquier propiedad y activos comprados con fondos públicos sean devueltos al Distrito".</p><p>Un abogado y funcionarios de Aspira no respondieron a una solicitud de comentarios.</p><p>Aspira de Illinois tuvo problemas financieros en marzo y fue obligada a cerrar dos escuelas chárter en el vecindario de Avondale, en el lado noroeste de la ciudad. Más de 500 estudiantes tuvieron que encontrar nuevos lugares donde estudiar a mitad del año escolar. Y la moderna escuela de Aspira en Milwaukee y Monticello quedó vacía.</p><p>Aspira se declaró en bancarrota en junio y, alrededor de un mes después, pidió a la corte permiso para vender el edificio por $11 millones.</p><p>Los funcionarios de Aspira explicaron en documentos de la corte que el dinero se usaría para pagar una hipoteca de $5.8 millones sobre un edificio más pequeño y antiguo, así como aproximadamente $1.5 millones en deudas con varios acreedores, incluyendo el Fondo de Pensiones de los Maestros de Chicago.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Cuando Aspira puso a la venta su antigua secundaria, el anuncio de la propiedad aseguraba que el edificio permanecía en condiciones impecables.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times file</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Pero los funcionarios de Aspira también indicaron en los registros de la corte que planeaban usar el resto del dinero para seguir operando de alguna manera. La organización aún administra una escuela alternativa financiada por CPS, y la directora ejecutiva interina de Aspira dijo en un comunicado el mes pasado que, de ahora en adelante, la organización se enfocará en "reconstruirse y cambiar de imagen".</p><p>La reclamación de CPS sobre parte de las ganancias de la venta probablemente se basa en su contrato con Aspira, que establece que si la organización sin fines de lucro dejara de operar sus escuelas, la organización "deberá" devolver "cualquier propiedad o activos" comprados con fondos de CPS que se usaron para operar sus escuelas.</p><p>La ley estatal busca aclarar cualquier ambigüedad al decir que cualquier cosa "comprada con fondos públicos deberá ser devuelta al distrito escolar" del que la chárter obtuvo su inscripción.</p><p>Aunque el estado pagó la construcción del edificio que está a la venta, los funcionarios estatales no han respondido a preguntas sobre si reclamarán las ganancias, ni sus abogados se han presentado en la corte.</p><p>La cobertura de WBEZ y del Sun-Times parece haber cambiado la manera en que se manejará el dinero de la venta.</p><p>Cuando el abogado de Aspira, Paul Bach, compareció ante la corte la semana pasada buscando la aprobación de la venta, señaló que habló con el abogado de CPS después de que se publicara "un artículo de noticias que todo el mundo ha leído", en referencia a un reportaje de agosto de WBEZ y del Sun-Times.</p><p>Dijo que Aspira propuso un plan en el que pagaría algunas de sus deudas y pondría aproximadamente $4 millones en una cuenta en garantía, a la que la organización no podría acceder hasta que la corte decida qué debe hacerse con ese dinero.</p><p>Bach también abordó la cuestión de si $11 millones es un precio justo para un antiguo edificio escolar que costó $27 millones en fondos estatales para construirse. Cuando Aspira puso a la venta el edificio de Milwaukee Avenue, <a class="Link" href="https://images1.showcase.com/d2/RutaJhL163YxVze3jesqELgIqTH9LQRuJ30-mKM00F4/document.pdf" target="_blank" >el anuncio inmobiliario destacaba</a> que se mantiene en condición impecable y que ha tenido "inversiones de capital significativas" que apoyarían su "uso continuado o una reutilización adaptativa sin problemas".</p><p>Bach dijo a la corte que $11 millones era "por mucho, la mejor oferta que hemos recibido hasta la fecha" y que la siguiente oferta más cercana era de $7 millones.</p><p>Le pidió al juez no posponer la venta.</p><p>"Todo el objetivo es vender esta propiedad", dijo la semana pasada, señalando que cada mes que Aspira tiene que seguir pagando la hipoteca de su segundo edificio es "perjudicial", ya que reduce la cantidad de dinero que la organización tiene disponible.</p><p>Un abogado del Fondo de Pensiones de los Maestros de Chicago pidió a Aspira que aceptara una auditoría financiera. Las escuelas chárter deben cubrir parte de los beneficios de jubilación de su personal. Según documentos de la corte, Aspira le debe al fondo de pensiones más de $200,000.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de</i> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>
